label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Our payments partner froze withdrawals. Here's what happened, where your money is, and what we're doing**

Some of you have already noticed. Since Friday 6 November you can't take money out of Pinha, and deposits and round-ups have stopped too. Many of you have written to us, some in capitals. I've read every message. I'm angry about this too, and I want to say that before anything else.

I'm Inês, a product designer at Pinha. I write most of the words you see in the app. Rui, our CEO, is in calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal all day, so I'm writing this for him and for the team.

**What happened**

Pinha works with a payments partner called Northvale Payments, based in Vilnius. Northvale holds the money you've saved with us in a safeguarded account, kept separate from Northvale's own money. That setup exists so that a company going wrong doesn't take your money with it. We chose Northvale and we trusted them.

On 4 November, Northvale emailed to end our partnership with 30 days' notice. The only reason they gave was a "risk appetite review," which tells you nothing about what they actually think is wrong, if anything.

Two days later, on Thursday 6 November at 09:00, they blocked all outgoing transfers without warning, before their own 30 days were up. Deposits and round-ups stopped with them.

Northvale broke their own notice period. Calling that "risk" doesn't change what it is. We think it's cowardice, and we won't dress it up as anything else.

**Where your money is**

Your money is not lost. It sits in a safeguarded account, and as we understand it, Northvale cannot use it for their own purposes.

The hard part is that we can't move it either until Northvale releases it. Safe and available are not the same thing right now, and I know that's a painful thing to hear. I designed the screen in the app that says "your money is always yours, take it out anytime." I look at it now and feel sick. That promise was ours to keep, and we had no plan for when someone else controlled the money.

**What we got wrong**

We relied on one payments partner and had no backup. That was our mistake, not only theirs. We should have planned for exactly this. We're sorry.

**What we're doing**

We've already signed with a new partner, Ostra Bank in Lisbon. To move your balances there, Northvale has to send us the balance file, and Banco de Portugal has to approve the move. Neither of those is in our hands.

On 7 November we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Our estimate for the migration is 10 to 15 working days. That is an estimate, not a promise. We don't know when Northvale will act, and we won't give you a date we can't keep. When we know more, you'll hear it here first.

We're also trying to reach Northvale. Their account manager stopped answering calls on Friday, and their phone now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. We keep trying.

**What you can do now**

- **Monthly fee:** cancelled for November and December, for everyone. You won't be charged.
- **Support:** we've received about 1,900 emails since Friday, and a team of three is answering them. Replies are currently taking around two days. I'm sorry for the wait. Please don't resend the same message, because it slows everything down.
- **Urgent cases:** if you need money for rent, medical costs, or because you've lost your job, write to **urgent@pinha.example** with **URGENTE** in the subject line. We're trying to get individual releases for these cases. I can't promise an outcome for each one, but we are reading every urgent message.
- **Fixed deadlines:** if you have a payment you can't move, like a deposit or tuition, say what the deadline is in your email. It helps us prioritise.

One of you wrote to us about three years of saving for a car deposit, with the dealer's deadline on Friday 13 November. I read it on the metro and nearly cried. If you're in that position, please use the urgent address. We're pushing that case as hard as we can, and I won't pretend that's enough.

**What comes next**

We'll post an update here every Monday and Thursday until this is solved, even if the update is "no change yet." Silence would be worse.

You're allowed to be angry, at Northvale and at us for trusting a partner with no backup. I'm not going to tell you to calm down.

Inês
Product Designer, Pinha

---

**Notes before you publish:**

1. **Date:** you said Tuesday 10 November, but today is 11 November. Update the publication date, and check whether "Friday 13 November" still reads correctly.
2. **Legal check:** the post names Northvale and makes claims about safeguarding, the notice period, and "cowardice" while complaints are open with two regulators. Rui or your lawyers should review those lines, especially "cannot use it" and "broke their own notice," before it goes live.
3. **Porto case:** I kept it anonymous. Check that the person is fine with you referencing her message.

reasons: The publication notes instruct the user and interrupt the piece, and the post incorrectly calls 6 November Thursday rather than Friday.
